$comment: The single source of truth for the manual-testing checklist. docs/MANUAL-TESTING.md is generated from this file plus docs/MANUAL-TESTING.template.md; scripts/check-rows.mjs fails when the two disagree. A row is identified by section plus number - 14 and 15 each appear in two sections. status: automated (a test covers it), human (only a person can answer it), unrun (automatable, no test yet). A row whose automatable half is covered while the row as a whole still needs a person stays human and says so in `note`; `test` may still name what covers that half. `test` is a full mocha title; `tier` says where it is checked - "integration" (the default) means the title has to appear as a passing test in the run's own result files, "unit" means it is checked against the sources under test/unit, since the unit tier writes no result file.

rows.task: Install the `.vsix` in a clean profile, open the panel
rows.expected: Setup prompt appears, no error notification
rows.test: installed build first start activates a production installation without error
rows.note: Covered by its own launch against the packaged `.vsix`, never through the existing suite: `activate()` returns `{}` in production mode, so the test seams are empty there. The same suite also asserts the declared commands, the setting defaults and the MCP provider contribution; the named test is the one that proves the host is running an installed build at all.

rows.task: Run setup, choose `managed`
rows.expected: Binary lands in `~/.local/bin`, checksum verified, no terminal prompt; the Setup button fills with a percentage and reads "Installing..." past 90
rows.note: A real download to a real path with a real checksum.

rows.task: Disable the network, run setup
rows.expected: Clear error message, **no half-written binary left behind**
rows.note: Needs the network stack actually down; the harness has no network isolation control.

rows.task: After Setup, check the MCP server list and this installation's own `mcp.json` - the one beside its `globalStorage`
rows.expected: "Codebase Memory" is listed as coming from this extension and starts; the file holds **no** `codebase-memory-mcp` key, not even right after Setup ran the CLI's `install`
rows.test: extension activation contributes an MCP server definition provider the host supports
rows.note: The `mcp.json` half is covered at the unit tier by `withoutMcpEntry`; the contribution point is covered here.

rows.task: With an older managed binary, restart
rows.expected: Update offer appears and applies; Windows update succeeds while the server runs
rows.test: updating the managed binary completes an update from a real older build while its server runs

rows.task: Lock the target file, then update
rows.expected: Old binary restored, error explains where the backup is
rows.test: updating the managed binary rolls back and leaves the older installation intact when the target is locked
rows.note: Windows file locking has no POSIX equivalent, so the test is registered on Windows only.

rows.task: Set `binarySource` to `external`, point at your own install
rows.expected: No update button, no install button, panel still lists projects
rows.test: an external binary offers no Setup and no Update button, and still lists projects
rows.note: Config update plus `panelHtmlForTests()`, the shape `update-check.test.ts` already uses. The pinned binary is what makes it more than a config toggle: `external` with nothing to point at resolves to the needs-setup screen, which would satisfy an assertion about the update button for the wrong reason, so the test also asserts the panel reports the source as external.

rows.task: Open a repository, look at the project list
rows.expected: Workspace is **not** listed as a project by itself
rows.test: an open repository is not treated as a project does not render the open folder as a project card

rows.task: Add several folders at once
rows.expected: All indexed, `workspaceFolders` unchanged, no folder added to the workspace
rows.test: commands behind a modal dialog opens a folder picker for add repositories, and a dismissal is a no-op

rows.task: Remove a project
rows.expected: Confirmation mentions the index only, never the workspace
rows.test: commands behind a modal dialog names the project in the confirmation, and a dismissal never reaches the CLI

rows.task: Add a `codebase-memory-mcp` entry to `mcp.json` by hand and reload
rows.expected: The provided server and the hand-written one appear side by side as separate servers; the extension does not remove the entry outside its own `install` call
rows.test: removes our own entry and leaves every other server in place
rows.note: Covered at the unit tier against `withoutMcpEntry`. An integration version would be racy and vacuous: the guard only rewrites an `mcp.json` that already exists.

rows.task: With Settings Sync enabled on a Windows and a macOS machine, run Setup on both and use the server on each
rows.expected: Both work at once and neither inherits the other's absolute path; `mcp.json` carries no entry of ours on either machine, so there is nothing to ping-pong
rows.note: Inherently cross-machine and live, and easy to run in a way that measures nothing if the two profiles never actually sync.

rows.task: Switch `binarySource`, or take an update, without reloading the window
rows.expected: The provided server carries the new binary - VS Code offers to refresh the tools rather than requiring a window reload
rows.note: `vscode.lm.mcpServerDefinitions` is behind an API proposal and throws when read, so the row is human as specified.

rows.task: With a CLI 0.10.x engine running (any CLI call starts its daemon), take an update from the panel
rows.expected: The panel does not warn about a surviving daemon, the project list still renders, and reindex works without a window reload
rows.test: updating the managed binary stops a 0.10.x daemon as part of the update

rows.task: Against a 0.10.x binary, look at an indexed git checkout, then commit in it and refresh
rows.expected: The card shows the branch, and the project is reported as outdated after the checkout moves
rows.test: branch and staleness of an indexed checkout reports the project outdated once the checkout moves on
rows.note: Two tests in `branch-staleness.test.ts`: "names the branch the project was indexed from" covers the first half, and the named one covers the second. The panel markup is the observable rather than the log line, which says "outdated" only once per change.

rows.task: Uninstall the extension
rows.expected: No terminal opens; copy-command hint discoverable in the README
rows.test: extension activation copies a runnable betterCmm.copyUninstallCommand string for this platform
rows.note: The no-terminal half is automated; README discoverability is the human half.

rows.task: Run the copy-uninstall and copy-daemon-stop commands on Windows, macOS, Linux
rows.expected: Correct string in the clipboard on each, and the pasted line runs in the shell it is labelled for
rows.test: extension activation copies a runnable betterCmm.copyDaemonStopCommand string for this platform
rows.note: The clipboard contents are automated per OS; that the pasted line actually runs in the shell it is labelled for is the human half - the bug class this row has already found twice.

rows.task: Switch light, dark, high contrast themes
rows.expected: Readable, no unstyled flash, no horizontal scrollbar

rows.task: Index a repository with >10,000 files
rows.expected: Panel responsive, statistics update, no editor freeze
rows.note: The indexing half is bounded by the 240 s assertion in `panel-render.test.ts` - 12,000 files added 21 s, a real 17-project reindex took 77.6 s. Responsiveness itself stays human: the bound measures a command, not the UI.

rows.task: Leave VS Code open with the panel hidden for an hour
rows.expected: No CLI processes spawned while hidden
rows.test: idle cost with the panel hidden launches no CLI while the panel is hidden, and keeps ticking
